quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: It is illegal to operate a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: In California, drivers age 21 or older cannot operate a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Drivers under 21 cannot operate a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. It is unsafe to ride even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use both front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to make the motorcycle more stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it could cause the bike to tip. Instead, use the rear brake to control your speed during the U-turn.

questions.question: When choosing a jacket for protection, it should:

options.text: Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Not be made of leather or another sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Your jacket and pants should be made of leather or another strong material. They should fit snugly enough that they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should stay at least this many seconds behind the vehicle ahead:
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. If conditions are poor, increase this distance.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does "SEE" stand for?
questions.explanation: Experienced riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions while riding. "SEE" stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic will merge.

questions.question: Which factor affects a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: The three main factors that affect BAC are how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, the best way to help others see your motorcycle is:

options.text: Keep your high beam headlight turned on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight turned on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on. Use your high beam both day and night whenever it is legal and safe.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have footrests for passengers. Good foot placement keeps your passenger from falling off and pulling you down too.

questions.question: When riding at night, keep a minimum distance of:
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances in the dark. When riding at night, stay at least three seconds behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little faster than normal
Start slowing down earlier than normal
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes your motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing down earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger gaps in traffic when carrying a passenger.

questions.question: To be seen better, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or when visibility is poor
Add an orange tint to your headlight

questions.explanation: Using your headlight at all times is the best way to help others see your motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, motorcyclists should:
questions.explanation: Riding in a staggered formation keeps the group close while giving each rider enough space. Switch to a single-file line when turning, going through curves, or entering or leaving the road.

questions.question: If you are riding behind another vehicle at night, you can see bumps on the road ahead by:

options.text: Listening for the vehicle scraping the pavement
Watching the vehicle's taillights bounce up and down
Looking at the vehicle's rear bumper and seeing if it bounces

questions.correctAnswerText: Watching the vehicle's taillights bounce up and down
questions.explanation: At night, use the vehicle ahead of you to see road conditions. If its taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps on the road ahead.

questions.question: Before riding, check your clutch. A working clutch should feel:
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should spring back when you release it, and the clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to start moving
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with flashing lights, move to a different lane to give it space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle takes:

options.text: Less time than usual to stop and speed up
The same amount of time to stop and speed up
More time than usual to stop and speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: More time than usual to stop and speed up
questions.explanation: Extra weight makes your motorcycle slower to accelerate and decelerate. Your motorcycle will respond more slowly when you carry a passenger than when you ride alone.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to maintain control in a turn?
questions.explanation: To stay in control during a turn, slow down before entering it. Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Lean into the turn and roll on the throttle to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: To be seen more easily by other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you. This works at any time of day.

questions.question: A main cause of single-motorcycle crashes is:

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve.
Leaving the road to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-motorcycle crashes is turning too wide in curves. This can make your motorcycle leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, during a crash. A windshield alone is not enough.

questions.question: Using both brakes:

options.text: Should be done every time you stop.
Should only be done in emergencies.
Should only be done on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done every time you stop.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Do not wait for emergencies.

questions.question: Eye protection:

options.text: Is not needed if your motorcycle has a windshield.
Is only needed in bad weather.
Should let you see clearly to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should let you see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: Eye protection is required by law in California. A good face shield must allow you to see clearly to both sides.
